title: Fix LightmapGI shadow leaks
body:
Fixes shadow leaks | Before | After | |--------|--------| | ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19e5ccbc-ef34-4ed6-8e81-620b401d3fab) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09312a52-488f-44eb-849f-f1f6d9860693) | Test project: [shadowleaks.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20646426/shadowleaks.zip) Lightmapper already does unocclusion pass to hide dark semi-occluded texels (inspired by [bakery approach](https://ndotl.wordpress.com/2018/08/29/baking-artifact-free-lightmaps/)), but all of that work becomes undone when you enable denoiser. Denoiser is unaware of what's occluded and what isn't so it samples from occluded black texels which results in shadow leaks. This PR solves the issue by using unocclusion pass as a mask to prevent denoiser from sampling occluded texels. | Lightmap | Occlusion mask | Blender Cycles for comparison | |--------|--------|--------| | ![lightmap2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab5b6caf-bb69-4fcf-a7f1-ee1f688d7d68) | ![mask](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/037a23ea-286c-4046-ba1a-b1e72f1f6c4f) | ![cycles](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/258c18d6-cb86-4543-8d7b-2573c7cbcf66) | > [!NOTE] > Under some conditions it's easy to mistake shadowleaks for AO. However unlike AO this doesn't happen in all crevices, only in places where geometry intersects. It's also resolution-dependent, angle-independent, and can leak asymmetrically on 2 adjacent surfaces. If you're interested in additional baked AO for creative purposes (and which you have control over) I opened a [proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10607) for that last year > [!NOTE] > OIDN has this issue too, though to a lesser extent (leaks are much thinner). It's third-party though so not much can be done. I recommend using JNLM, it gives great results
⚠️ Important information for testing:

Keep in mind that your geometry needs to have backface culling enabled for godot lightmapper to work properly. While this is important for the fix in this PR to work properly, this isn't specific only to this PR. If you have double-sided materials godot won't be able to do even the basic 1-texel unocclusion that it already does. Here's comparison of one-sided vs double-sided material in the current **master** branch with denoiser disabled. Notice that there are both light leaks and shadow leaks here caused by light reaching surfaces that it shouldn't and unocclusion algorithm not being able to do its job properly: ![culling](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d44aeb1d-665f-4ee2-a6d7-2d6e5b1a4ec6) If you're importing textured meshes from Blender you can make sure backface culling is enabled in the material properties: ![culling2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/663ea6cc-47b8-4f91-a927-1702ca4ee9cf)
